column1: # patch-limits.csv -- PROVISIONAL windows for the analog patch station (S121).
# PW tunes these; d24_patch.py reads nothing else and carries no number of its own.
# NOTHING HERE IS A SPEC LIMIT. Each one is either a ratio that follows from how the

column2: or a placeholder waiting on a good unit. `source` says which.

column4: source

the harness revision's own figure for the same check (runner-interface.md, 'Detecting a wrong connection'): the measured lane must rise at least this far above its idle floor before a reading is called a tone at all

runner-interface.md condition 2: every input other than the one under test stays at least this far below it. A single switch pair isolates about -99 dB at 1 kHz, so 40 dB is a wide gate that only a real mis-patch or a crossed pair can fail

AUTO-ADVANCE, tone rows: how far the expected lane's meter must rise over its unplugged baseline before the step is called done. Well under tone_min_over_floor_db on purpose -- this ends the operator's step, the measurement that follows decides the verdict

AUTO-ADVANCE, noise rows (S153): read on the measurement node's RMS, not the strip meter. The 150 ohm swap is two moves -- the tone lead out (the input goes OPEN) and the plug in (TERMINATED) -- and the step ends when the lane has settled this far below BOTH the lead it was prompted with and the open input it was pulled to. STILL PROVISIONAL, not set from a good unit: the open-vs-terminated margin at gain 63 is 5.9-13.3 dB on 15 of the 16 surveyed channels (S125 open against S55 terminated, different days), MIC 6 is 1.1 dB on S55's node figure and 6.6 on its capture, and MIC 1-4 and 13-16 have never been measured open or terminated. A channel under this margin does not advance: it raises the no-signal question at detect_timeout_s
how long a patch waits before the runner sweeps every lane to find where the lead actually went

AUX A 1-2/3-4/5-6/7-8 TRS (P63-P66), one leg against the lane's balanced XLR reference (S164). DERIVED, not assumed: each tip/ring is the matching rear XLR OUT_n re-received single-ended by one NJM4580L on the phone-jack board (U1..U8: unit B a difference amp, R43/R45 = R44/R46 = 10k 0.1 %, unit A a follower, both driving the jack through 33R; mx26 docs/d24-analog-paths.md + BOM D24 Phone Jack rev B), so the tip carries hot minus cold = the FULL balanced level: 0 dB, not the -6.02 one-leg guess. NOT the AK4619 (that codec drives only the panel speaker on a D24). Loading cannot move it: 33R build-outs on both stages. Measured on MW-D24-2: -1.42 dB (P63 L, factory pass 5, 2026-10-01) and -0.8 dB (hand check 2026-09-30, AUX 1 XLR vs AUX A TRS into MIC 3) -- inside level_tol_db, unexplained by the stage; the resume's four jacks cross-check it

front PHONES jack J10 (S164), one leg against the lane's balanced XLR reference. nan = RECORDED, NOT JUDGED until a unit has measured it: no phones level has ever been read. Prediction from the netlist + analog BOM: U92 (AK4458) ch1/2 -> 2 x 1k -> NJM4580M U90/U91 multiple-feedback low-pass, 6k2/2k = 3.1 on the DAC differential, i.e. half the XLR stage's balanced 6.2 -> -6.02 dB; BUT the netlist puts U90.5/U91.5 (+in) on GND with the mirror network (R1982/C843) floating, and built that way the stage takes one DAC leg only -> -12.04 dB. MONITOR L/R (J53/J54) read -26.2 dB against the XLR on pass 4, also unexplained. Fill in from the first unit's reading (patch-results / factory.log P67) and the window applies from then on

the window around each single-ended key above (trs_aux_out_db, phones_out_db). Wide enough to pass the unexplained -1.4 dB on AUX A, narrow enough to catch a dead or halved path. Tighten from a good unit
the two sub-tests of one stereo jack share everything but the channel, so they must match each other far more tightly than either matches the absolute window

the null sub-test, relative to the same jack's single-ended reading. What is left is the L/R match of the output stage plus the lead. A crossed or absent channel cannot reach this; a good unit sets the real figure

how the measured phase is turned into normal/inverted: within this of the lane's reference phase is normal, beyond it is inverted. 90 deg is the decision boundary itself, so a reading near it is reported as UNCERTAIN rather than guessed
a reading within this of the 90 deg boundary is UNCERTAIN, not a verdict

THE SEVEN GAIN STEPS (PW 2026-09-27): how far a step's MEASURED gain may sit from its expected value before the step is called wrong. PW ruling, S129 addendum 5 -- "gain step resistors should fall within +/- 0.25dB to pass", tightened 12x from the provisional 3.0 dB of 2026-09-26 now that a good unit has been walked. The expected values are in patch-gain-steps.csv: defs' own measured mic gain law where it carries the code, a six-element fit of that same law where it does not. THE FIT'S WORST RESIDUAL IS 0.51 dB, which is TWICE this window, so on the four FITTED codes (8/16/32 and the 63 EIN step) the expected value is not yet good enough to judge against 0.25 dB and the measurement is not what would be failing -- see the S129 report. A 1 % resistor is +/-0.09 dB on its own, so tolerance alone eats a third of the budget

how long the chain image is left to act before a gain step is read. The preamp gain follows the CS_M latch by about 10 ms (S70-7 / the 09-26 bench note), so 50 ms is five times the hardware's own delay. PROVISIONAL: the cheapest honest number, and the one the step time is built on

INPUT HEADROOM (PW 2026-10-01, S164): headroom = the input level at which THD+N reaches 1 % = -40 dB, read off the measurement node at gain code 0, in dBu at the connector (drive dBFS + units.csv dac_fs_dbu, the AUX 1 XLR full scale) and in dBFS at the converter. Reported in dB and %
the drive the ramp starts at: the station's own tone level, about -6.5 dBFS on a code-0 lane (loop gain +5.5 dB), so the first step is clean
the ramp's step. PW: small steps. The 1 % crossing is interpolated linearly in dB between the last step under it and the first at or over it, and the crossing step is read twice
the ramp's ceiling: DAC full scale on AUX 1 (+23.1 dBu). The outputs swing about 5.6 dB more than an input takes, so an input reaches 1 % well before this; a ramp that hits it records 'not reached'

THE REFERENCE: the AVERAGE of every input's 1 % THD level from the first pass that measured them (PW ruling 2026-10-01), excluding and naming any input more than headroom_exclude_db from the median. nan = this pass RECORDS and does not grade. Written by tools/accept/headroom_ref.py from the run's state.json, with the source pass in this column, and the per-input values as headroom_micNN_dbu
PROVISIONAL (PW to confirm): an input whose 1 % THD level is more than this BELOW headroom_ref_dbu fails. Above it never fails
an input more than this from the median of the pass is left out of the average and named (PW ruling 2026-10-01)
